static_traits.name: Chen Xinya
static_traits.family_status: Grew up in a military family; parents' situation not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive group of friends, but not yet discussing surfing-related distress with them; friends have noticed changes in mood and behavior
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems appeared before, never received psychological counseling or treatment; no major physical illness history
static_traits.language_features: Good cooperativeness, positive attitude; able to self-reflect and cognitively restructure; clear expression, good logic; speech rate not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: After being knocked over by a big wave while surfing at sea, I have persistently felt failure and disappointment, developing the thought 'I can never become an elite surfer'; the event was accompanied by high stress and shame at the time, along with dismissing past positive surfing experiences and a tendency to overgeneralize my ability from a single event.
basic_info.core_demands: Negative thoughts and feelings of failure affected self-esteem and enjoyment of surfing, so seeks counseling to help challenge and restructure these negative thoughts and restore a more balanced and realistic view of self.
growth_experiences: Grew up in a military family (parents' specific situation and parenting style not mentioned).

special_situations.event: While surfing big waves at the beach, was overturned by a wave and felt seen and judged by many
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make an obvious mistake in front of others, it proves I am not good enough / am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding talking about the event with friends to avoid being judged and not being understood
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never become an elite surfer

special_situations.event: After each high-difficulty surfing training or challenging sea conditions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure can define my overall ability and future performance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replaying the failure scene, immersing in Self-doubt in an attempt to 'prevent failing again'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This failure shows I am bad at surfing

special_situations.event: Recalling past successful surfing experiences or receiving others' praise
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only stable and perfect success counts; occasional success has no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Attributing positive performance to 'just luck', to maintain a consistent negative self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That was just luck; these successes are not important

special_situations.event: Has made mistakes in public or recalls scenes of being watched by others
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are present, they will watch and negatively evaluate my performance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing contact with external feedback as self-protection (e.g. not discussing surfing distress with friends)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are all looking at me and think I am terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and to prove they are good enough (performing well in important domains such as surfing)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failing in front of the public and being humiliated and judged by others, thereby defining oneself as a 'failure'
defense_goal: Maintaining distance and silence (not revealing surfing distress to friends) to reduce the risk of being judged
Dismissing positive evidence by attributing positive experiences to 'luck', lowering expectations to reduce disappointment

object_relations.self_representation: A humiliated failure, a not-good-enough self
A help-seeker hesitant for fear of being misunderstood
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may not understand and may think I am overreacting (though friends are generally supportive in reality)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reminded by the counselor or others of past successes, or invited to view the current setback from a positive perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing those successes are not real or not important (transference: projecting my own unworthiness and shame experiences onto external feedback)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplays positive evidence, emphasizes 'just luck'; calm tone but slightly self-critical, replacing emotional expression with factual explanations.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling surfing mistakes in public settings, or feeling watched and judged by others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to attribute inner shame and unworthiness to others' negative views ('They think I am bad')
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using expressions that guess others' thoughts (e.g. 'they must be looking down on me'), in a tense, defensive tone.

manifestations: Feeling watched and judged for failing in public, developing shame and withdrawal
Not talking about specific surfing distress with the supportive friend group; inner experience relatively isolated
outcomes: Lacks motivation for other interests (e.g. baking)

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-Reflection and introspection ability, including Excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Harshly blaming myself with self-labels like 'I am a failure' and 'I am not good enough'
Not daring to seek help for fear friends will not understand or think I am overreacting
In conversation, quickly explains positive experiences as 'just luck'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Feels everyone is watching and judging her
Attributing shame and unworthiness to others' negative evaluations

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains behavioral impulses toward other people or the environment, and instead acts on the self, or withdraws the energy inward.
manifestations: Not discussing surfing-related distress with supportive friends
Internalizing stress, developing sleep disturbance and low mood

exception_events.target_problem: After experiencing challenging surfing training, the client usually overgeneralizes one mistake as overall inadequacy, falling into disappointment and Self-doubt.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In past difficult surfing training, the client learned from setbacks and gradually improved performance, rather than being completely defined by failure.
exception_events.reason: Different understanding: viewing difficult situations as learning opportunities ('everyone has days with mistakes'), thereby preserving room for improvement and building up experience.

positive_force: Has a supportive group of friends
Past experience of being able to learn and improve in difficult surfing
Overall good occupational functioning (stable nursing work ability)
negative_force: Dismissing positive evidence (attributing success to 'just luck')
Negative predictions about future surfing leading to anxiety and disturbed sleep

target_behavior.behavior: Engaging in negative rumination after surfing mistakes (catastrophizing, overgeneralizing, dismissing positive evidence) and self-labeling as a 'failure'
antecedent: Public mistake situations such as being overturned by big waves at sea
Recalls scenes of being watched and judged by others
target_behavior.core_reason: Self-esteem and self-worth are highly sensitive to performance, accompanied by high worry about others' evaluations and a sense of shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping the emotions of failure and shame, trying to obtain a sense of control through self-criticism or to avoid setbacks again
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-esteem, disturbed sleep, reduced interest (e.g. baking), declining work attention and performance

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance (not discussing surfing distress with supportive friends)
antecedent: Shame experienced after feeling watched and judged
Worrying friends will not understand or will think I am overreacting
target_behavior.core_reason: Fears negative evaluation and being misunderstood, maintaining safety by keeping silent
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential dismissive feedback and embarrassing emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Support resources not yet used; negative emotions and cognitions persist; recovery slows down
